about.japanDescription:
Biwako International Trading LTD is a Japan-based wholesale exporter of used Japanese auto parts, operating from Imizu City, Toyama Prefecture, since 2003. Over more than two decades, we have built a trusted reputation as a reliable B2B supplier of half cut cars, CKD vehicles, used engines, bulk spare parts, and complete vehicle exports by container and RoRo shipping. Our clients — auto dealers, dismantlers, and importers across Russia, Mongolia, the Philippines, Africa, and Pacific Island nations — rely on Biwako for competitive pricing, rigorous quality inspection, and dependable logistics tailored to each destination market.

Every shipment we prepare is the result of a careful sourcing process that begins at Japan’s professional vehicle auction network. We purchase vehicles, dismantle or cut them to our clients’ specifications, and pack 20ft or 40ft containers with maximum efficiency. Whether you need a single engine or a full container of mixed parts, our team handles every step: sourcing, dismantling, cutting, quality checking, packing, loading, documentation, and sea freight — so your business receives exactly what it ordered, on time, at the right price.
article.import.body:
Japan maintains one of the world's strictest vehicle inspection systems, known as Shaken. This mandatory roadworthiness test, required every two years for most passenger vehicles, means that Japanese owners frequently replace vehicles that are still in excellent mechanical condition simply because the cost of passing inspection exceeds the vehicle's perceived value at that age. The result is a continuous and abundant supply of low-mileage, well-maintained vehicles entering Japan's used vehicle market every year — vehicles whose engines, transmissions, and components remain highly serviceable and carry far more remaining life than comparable second-hand parts from other markets.

Step 1: Define Your Requirements

Before contacting a Japanese exporter, clarify what you need. The more precise your specification, the faster and more accurately a reputable supplier can quote you. Key details to prepare:

  • Vehicle makes and models most in demand in your market
  • Specific engines or part types required
  • Preferred condition grade (based on Japanese auction grading)
  • Container format: half cut, CKD, bulk parts, or complete vehicle
  • Destination port and any known import regulations in your country
  • Approximate monthly or quarterly volume to negotiate better pricing

Step 2: Choose the Right Import Format

Your choice of import format significantly affects your landed cost, customs duty, and what you receive. The four main formats used for importing Japanese used parts by container are: bulk parts containers (individual used parts mixed or sorted), half cut containers (front or rear sections of vehicles), CKD containers (completely disassembled vehicles), and Rack & Stack containers (multiple compact vehicles dismantled and stacked). Each has different cost, duty, and reassembly implications depending on your destination country. A reputable supplier will advise you on the format that offers the best economics for your specific market.

Step 3: Select a Reputable Japanese Exporter

This is the most critical step. Key factors to evaluate when choosing a Japanese auto parts exporter:

  • Years in operation (established exporters have proven logistics and supplier networks)
  • Provision of Japanese auction sheets with every vehicle (non-negotiable for quality verification)
  • Transparency about quality grading and condition
  • Clear payment terms and professional invoicing
  • References or testimonials from clients in your region
  • Responsive and clear communication before you commit to an order

Biwako International Trading has been operating since 2003, holds all necessary licenses, has multilingual managers and has shipped thousands of containers worldwide.

Step 4: Confirm Your Order and Pay

Once you have agreed on product, price, container specification, and shipping terms, you will receive a proforma invoice. Standard payment for Japanese auto parts export is bank T/T (telegraphic transfer). Reputable exporters require a deposit to begin sourcing, with the balance due before or at container loading. Never pay the full amount upfront to a supplier you have not worked with before without conducting due diligence.

Step 5: Monitor Preparation and Loading

A professional exporter will keep you updated during the sourcing, cutting, inspection, and packing process. Request photos of key items where possible. Before the container is sealed, confirm the final packing list matches your order.

Step 6: Receive Your Documents and Track the Shipment

After the vessel departs, you will receive your shipping documents: Bill of Lading, Commercial Invoice, Packing List, and export certificate. Keep these documents safe as they are required for customs clearance in your country. Use the Bill of Lading number and vessel name to track your shipment online.

Step 7: Clear Customs and Take Delivery

Work with a licensed customs broker in your country to prepare your import declaration. Import duties and taxes will depend on your country's tariff schedule and the classification of the goods (parts versus complete vehicles). For CKD shipments, confirm the HS code classification with your broker before importing, as the duty rate can differ significantly from complete vehicle rates.

Contact us with your requirements and our team will respond within 24 hours, Monday to Saturday.

article.polukar.body:
If you have been looking for a cost-effective way to import high-quality Japanese mechanical components for your dismantling business, repair workshop, or auto parts retail operation, the term "half cut" has probably come up in your research. It is one of the most popular and practical formats for importing Japanese used vehicle components in bulk, and understanding exactly what a half cut includes, how it is prepared, and why it is so commercially valuable will help you make better purchasing decisions.

What Exactly Is a Half Cut?

A half cut is a Japanese vehicle that has been professionally cut at approximately the B-pillar — the vertical structural column between the front and rear doors of a four-door car. The result is two distinct sections: a front half and a rear half.

When auto parts exporters refer to a "half cut," they almost always mean the front half, which is by far the more commercially valuable section. A front half cut typically includes:

  • The complete engine and engine bay
  • The transmission (automatic or manual) and torque converter or clutch
  • The front subframe, suspension, steering rack, and front axle assemblies
  • The complete wiring harness from the engine to the dashboard and fuse box
  • The dashboard, instrument cluster, airbag system, and HVAC controls
  • The radiator, intercooler (if turbocharged), A/C condenser, and cooling fan
  • The fuel system components including the fuel injectors and ECU

Why Is the Half Cut So Popular?

The half cut format solves a fundamental problem for auto parts importers: how to ship the maximum number of valuable mechanical assemblies in the minimum container space, at the lowest per-unit cost.

A complete car takes up much more container space than a half cut and carries significant shipping cost per unit. An individual engine shipment, by contrast, is just one component without the surrounding assemblies. The half cut strikes the ideal balance: it is compact enough that 14 to 16 units fit in a standard 40ft container, yet it includes every major mechanical component the importer needs in a pre-assembled, tested configuration.

For dismantlers, the half cut delivers perhaps 30 to 50 individual sellable parts in a single unit. For repairers, it provides the entire front-end mechanical assembly needed for a major engine-bay repair or swap. For auto parts retailers, it is an efficient way to restock a wide range of components from a single vehicle.

Half Cut vs Nose Cut vs Full CKD

FormatCut PointPer 40ft ContainerBest For
Nose CutBehind engine bay18–20 unitsEngine-focused importers
Half CutB-pillar14–16 unitsDismantlers, repairers
Full CKDFully disassembled6–8 vehiclesAssembly workshops, duty reduction

Available Makes & Models

We regularly supply half cuts for: Toyota (Land Cruiser, Hilux Surf, Prado, Corolla, Camry, Alphard, Crown, Noah/Voxy), Nissan (Navara, Patrol, X-Trail, Serena, Skyline), Honda (CR-V, Fit, Step Wagon), Mitsubishi (Pajero, L200, Outlander, Delica), Subaru (Forester, Legacy, Impreza), Mazda, Isuzu, Suzuki, Daihatsu, and more. Availability depends on current auction supply.

Quality & Documentation

Each half cut sourced by Biwako International comes with a Japanese auction sheet documenting the original vehicle's condition grade, mileage, accident history, and interior/exterior rating. This transparency is a core part of our service and allows our clients to make informed purchasing decisions with confidence.

Need a half cut from Japan?

Tell us the make, model, engine code, and destination country. We will confirm availability, pricing, and the next available shipping date. Minimum: 1 × 20ft container.

article.stoimost.body:
One of the most common questions from importers: "How much does a container of auto parts from Japan cost?" The answer depends on several factors. In this article we break down what makes up the total price, compare 20- and 40-foot containers, and give practical money-saving tips.

What Makes Up the Container Cost

The total price of a parts container from Japan consists of several cost items:

Cost ItemDescription
Parts costAuction vehicle price + dismantling cost
PackagingProtective materials, pallets, fasteners
Container loadingLoading work at the warehouse in Japan
Ocean freightContainer delivery from Japan to destination port
Export documentsInvoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate
Customs dutiesDepends on HS code and cargo value
VATAs applicable in destination country
Broker feesCustoms clearance at destination
Delivery to warehouseFrom port to your warehouse
💡 Important: At Biwako we handle all Japan-side costs — purchasing, dismantling, packaging, loading and export documents. You pay only for the cargo and freight.

20-foot vs 40-foot Container — Which Is Better?

Parameter20 ft (TEU)40 ft (FEU)
Internal volume~33 m³~67 m³
Payloadup to 21 tonsup to 26 tons
Approx. number of engines15–20 pcs35–45 pcs
Ocean freight (Toyama → Vladivostok)lowerhigher, but cheaper per unit
Recommended forFirst order, testRegular wholesale purchases

Conclusion: A 40-foot container is more cost-effective per unit of cargo. For a first order or small business, a 20-foot container is optimal.

Additional Costs Often Overlooked

  • Demurrage — penalty for container idle time at port beyond the free period (usually 5–7 days free)
  • Storage at customs warehouse — if customs clearance is delayed
  • Cargo insurance — recommended, costs 0.3–0.5% of cargo value
  • Certification — may be required for certain types of parts

How to Save on Shipping Parts from Japan

  1. Order 40-foot containers — freight cost per unit of cargo is lower
  2. Plan orders in advance — rush shipments cost more
  3. Choose Vladivostok — the closest Russian port to Japan, minimum freight
  4. Work with a trusted supplier — avoid hidden fees and overpayments
  5. Optimize container contents — mix light and heavy parts to maximize volume utilization

Want to know the exact cost of your container?

Send us your parts list — we will calculate the cost for your request for free.

Get a Cost Estimate

Frequently Asked Questions About Cost

Can I get a cheaper container by working directly with an auction?

No. Japanese auctions only work with licensed dealers. Without a license you cannot participate in bidding. That is why you need a reliable intermediary — a licensed exporter like Biwako.

Is delivery to my warehouse included in the price?

We arrange delivery to the destination port. Delivery from the port to your warehouse is arranged by you or through our partner broker.

Tips for Forming a Wholesale Order

Additional certificates required by specific destination customs authorities can be arranged on request.
faq.paymentDocumentation.a3: Yes. Marine cargo insurance is available and recommended for all shipments. Please request insurance when placing your order and specify the insured value.
faq.paymentDocumentation.a4: Our minimum order is one 20ft standard container. We also accept 40ft container orders. We do not accept single-item orders at this time. We serve registered businesses only.
faq.paymentDocumentation.a5: A Japanese auction sheet is a standardised condition report issued by Japan's vehicle auction houses for every vehicle sold at auction. It records the vehicle's grade (0 to 5, with 4.5–5 being excellent), odometer reading, accident history, body condition diagram, and interior rating. We provide the original auction sheet for every vehicle.
